chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Husayn ibn Harithah, from Muyassar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not do business with a person of 'ahah (defect/impairment), for they are the most unjust of things.'

key_terms.أَظْلَمُ شَيْءٍ: The most unjust of things/entities; indicates extreme unfairness or oppression in the transaction.
key_terms.ذُو عَاهَةٍ: One with a defect or impairment; in trade context, often refers to a defective coin or a merchant known for short-changing.

ai.seo_question: What does 'dhul 'ahah' mean in Shia commercial jurisprudence and why are they considered unjust?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) within the chapter on trade ethics, defining *dhul 'ahah* as a party with a hidden defect or known dishonesty in commercial dealings. The Imam’s characterization of them as 'the most unjust' (*azlam shay'*) underscores the severity of their deception, which goes beyond simple unfairness to include a violation of trust (*amanah*) and fair exchange (*mithl*). This ruling serves as a practical guideline for merchants to avoid partners whose inherent flaws compromise the integrity of the transaction.
